answer:
Use a uniform finite-volume grid with Nx=400 cells on the spatial domain [-1,1].
Set dx=2.0/Nx=0.005 and define cell centers as x_j=-1+(j+0.5)*dx for j=0,...,Nx-1.
Evolve the cell-averaged conservative variables U=[rho, m, E] where m=rho*v and E=p/(Gamma-1)+0.5*rho*v^2.
Use Gamma=1.6666666666666667, eta=0.1, zeta=0.1, and CFL=0.5.
Compute pressure from the equation of state p=(Gamma-1)*(E-0.5*m^2/rho) and enforce positivity by clipping rho and p to a small floor of 1e-12 if needed.
Use periodic boundary conditions by wrapping ghost cell indices, with the domain treated as periodic on x=-1 and x=1.
Use the Rusanov (local Lax-Friedrichs) numerical flux for the inviscid Euler part with interface wave speed a=max(|v_L|+c_L, |v_R|+c_R) and c=sqrt(Gamma*p/rho).
Compute the viscous stress sigma=(zeta+4/3*eta)*v_x using a centered difference on the cell-centered v values.
Approximate sigma at interfaces by averaging neighboring cell-centered sigma values.
Add viscous flux contributions F_visc=[0, -sigma, -v*sigma] at interfaces using interface-averaged v and sigma.
Use total interface flux F_total=F_hat+F_visc.
Use 2-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun's method) for time integration.
Choose the time step each step as dt=min(CFL*dx/max_j(|v_j|+c_j), 0.5*dx^2/max(zeta+4/3*eta, 1e-30)) and adjust the last step to hit T=0.5 exactly.
Run the simulation from t=0 to T=0.5.
Compute rho(x,T), v(x,T), and p(x,T) on the cell centers.
Save the file "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz" containing arrays x (1D length Nx), rho (1D), v (1D), p (1D), and scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, CFL.
Save a 3-panel line plot of rho, v, and p versus x at time T as "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png".
Print the min and max of rho and p as a positivity check, and print the mean of rho over the domain as a mass conservation check.
